text:
maria: Quick question — we're debating score serialization for the rerank endpoint. Do we send normalized probs (0..1), raw logits, or both?
aj: normalized probs by default. easier for clients and dashboards. logits are useful for debugging but dangerous if consumers assume prob semantics.
sam: +1 for probs. also we should include per-candidate metadata (e.g., explanation tags) but keep it optional to avoid bloat.
devon: what about size/limit implications? some customers fan out 500 candidates per request. Charging + batching will blow up.
rachel: we already have the 64KB payload soft-limit on console ingest. for rerank we should cap candidates per-call in API (e.g., 200) and document cost.
maria: proposal: default "scores": [0.0-1.0], optional field "logits" available if caller sets header `X-Rerank-Enable-Logits: true` (canary only). include `meta` per candidate as map<string,string> but capped keys to 16 and keys length limited.
aj: can we make `meta` an array of short tags instead of map to prevent huge allocations? e.g., `tags": ["reason:dup","source:bm25"]`
sam: good call. arrays cheaper to parse and smaller on wire.
devon: for huge fanouts, we should support streaming chunked responses and an envelope like: ```
{
  "model":"reranker-v3",
  "scores_chunk": [ ... ],
  "chunk_index": 0,
  "more": true
}
```
rachel: console UX note: we want to show score distribution (histogram) per-tenant and per-model; normalized probs make this easier. we also want a small sample of the top-k candidates with their tags.
maria: telemetry: track metric `rerank.request.candidates` (count), `rerank.score.dist.{bucket}` (histogram), `rerank.format.usage` (legacy|v2|logits), `rerank.backend_latency_ms` (p50/p95/p99) and `rerank.backoff.count` for fallback routing.
aj: routing: if preferred model is down, fallback to cheaper model variant but we need to mark scores as `inferred_from: model-v2-fallback`. include `score_origin` at envelope level.
sam: quota semantics: should we bill by candidates scored or by request? I vote candidates — aligns with cost. But customers may prefer per-request predictability. maybe support both: tenant-level setting defaulting to `candidates` billing.
devon: compatibility/rollout plan: support legacy shape and new shape. Add response header `X-Score-Encoding: v2` and accept client header `Accept-Score-Encoding: v2` for canaries. Log samples of legacy vs v2 for 1% of traffic. After 90 days, warn via console and deprecate legacy.
rachel: console should show a migration dashboard: percent clients on v2, top tenants still using legacy, sampling of malformed payloads, and a button to open support ticket.
maria: edgecase: some clients gzip the request body and proxies strip `Accept-Score-Encoding`. fallback negotiation must rely on presence of `X-Client-Announce: rerank-v2` in request body as a fallback.
aj: also consider signed scores for integrity in multi-tenant shared endpoints: optional `signed_score` field with an HMAC snippet.
sam: ops: we need throttles per-model and per-tenant. If we start charging by candidate, we need to expose a preview API that estimates candidate-units for a request without executing.
devon: implementation detail: runtime can store score arrays as float16 on wire using base64 to save cost for huge batches. add `score_encoding: "fp16-base64"` option. concern: client parsing complexity.
rachel: UX compromise: expose a toggle in the console that previews compressed payload and shows estimated parse time.
maria: final ask — can eng-platform + console team agree on a rollout checklist: 1) wire format v2 spec PR, 2) canary header handling, 3) telemetry metrics added (list above), 4) console migration dashboard, 5) 90-day deprecation notices, 6) sample logs to SRE for fallback behavior.
aj: I can pick up telemetry + billing hooks.
sam: I can do API shape and lib updates.
devon: I will prototype streaming chunked responses and fp16 encoding.
rachel: I'll design the migration dashboard mock tomorrow.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for rerank-encoding-v2 completed in prod-us-west-2 :tada:
maria: awesome. please leave any open questions here — I'll open the spec PR in the next hour. :eyes:
